paragraphs.text: In that hour came the disciples unto Jesus, saying, Who then is greatest in the kingdom of heaven?
paragraphs.original: Ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ προσῆλθον οἱ μαθηταὶ τῷ Ἰησοῦ λέγοντες· Τίς ἄρα μείζων ἐστὶν ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τῶν οὐρανῶν;
paragraphs.translit: En ekeinē tē hōra prosēlthon hoi mathētai tō Iēsou legontes· Tis ara meizōn estin en tē basileia tōn ouranōn;

paragraphs.text: And he called to him a little child, and set him in the midst of them,
paragraphs.original: καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος παιδίον ἔστησεν αὐτὸ ἐν μέσῳ αὐτῶν
paragraphs.translit: kai proskalesamenos paidion estēsen auto en mesō autōn

paragraphs.text: and said, Verily I say unto you, Except ye turn, and become as little children, ye shall in no wise enter into the kingdom of heaven.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἶπεν· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἐὰν μὴ στραφῆτε καὶ γένησθε ὡς τὰ παιδία, οὐ μὴ εἰσέλθητε εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν.
paragraphs.translit: kai eipen· Amēn legō hymin, ean mē straphēte kai genēsthe hōs ta paidia, ou mē eiselthēte eis tēn basileian tōn ouranōn.

paragraphs.text: Whosoever therefore shall humble himself as this little child, the same is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven.
paragraphs.original: ὅστις οὖν ταπεινώσει ἑαυτὸν ὡς τὸ παιδίον τοῦτο, οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ μείζων ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τῶν οὐρανῶν·
paragraphs.translit: hostis oun tapeinōsei heauton hōs to paidion touto, houtos estin ho meizōn en tē basileia tōn ouranōn·

paragraphs.text: And whoso shall receive one such little child in my name receiveth me:
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὃς ἐὰν δέξηται ἓν παιδίον τοιοῦτο ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματί μου, ἐμὲ δέχεται.
paragraphs.translit: kai hos ean dexētai hen paidion toiouto epi tō onomati mou, eme dechetai.

paragraphs.text: But whoso shall cause one of these little ones that believe on me to stumble, it is profitable for him that a great millstone should be hanged about his neck, and [that] he should be sunk in the depth of the sea.
paragraphs.original: Ὃς δʼ ἂν σκανδαλίσῃ ἕνα τῶν μικρῶν τούτων τῶν πιστευόντων εἰς ἐμέ, συμφέρει αὐτῷ ἵνα κρεμασθῇ μύλος ὀνικὸς εἰς τὸν τράχηλον αὐτοῦ καὶ καταποντισθῇ ἐν τῷ πελάγει τῆς θαλάσσης.
paragraphs.translit: Hos dʼ an skandalisē hena tōn mikrōn toutōn tōn pisteuontōn eis eme, sympherei autō hina kremasthē mylos onikos eis ton trachēlon autou kai katapontisthē en tō pelagei tēs thalassēs.

paragraphs.text: Woe unto the world because of occasions of stumbling! for it must needs be that the occasions come; but woe to that man through whom the occasion cometh!
paragraphs.original: οὐαὶ τῷ κόσμῳ ἀπὸ τῶν σκανδάλων· ἀνάγκη γὰρ ἐλθεῖν τὰ σκάνδαλα, πλὴν οὐαὶ τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ διʼ οὗ τὸ σκάνδαλον ἔρχεται.
paragraphs.translit: ouai tō kosmō apo tōn skandalōn· anankē gar elthein ta skandala, plēn ouai tō anthrōpō diʼ hou to skandalon erchetai.

paragraphs.text: And if thy hand or thy foot causeth thee to stumble, cut it off, and cast it from thee: it is good for thee to enter into life maimed or halt, rather than having two hands or two feet to be cast into the eternal fire.
paragraphs.original: Εἰ δὲ ἡ χείρ σου ἢ ὁ πούς σου σκανδαλίζει σε, ἔκκοψον αὐτὸν καὶ βάλε ἀπὸ σοῦ· καλόν σοί ἐστιν εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν ζωὴν κυλλὸν ἢ χωλόν, ἢ δύο χεῖρας ἢ δύο πόδας ἔχοντα βληθῆναι εἰς τὸ πῦρ τὸ αἰώνιον.
paragraphs.translit: Ei de hē cheir sou ē ho pous sou skandalizei se, ekkopson auton kai bale apo sou· kalon soi estin eiselthein eis tēn zōēn kyllon ē chōlon, ē dyo cheiras ē dyo podas echonta blēthēnai eis to pyr to aiōnion.

paragraphs.text: And if thine eye causeth thee to stumble, pluck it out, and cast it from thee: it is good for thee to enter into life with one eye, rather than having two eyes to be cast into the hell of fire.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἰ ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου σκανδαλίζει σε, ἔξελε αὐτὸν καὶ βάλε ἀπὸ σοῦ· καλόν σοί ἐστιν μονόφθαλμον εἰς τὴν ζωὴν εἰσελθεῖν, ἢ δύο ὀφθαλμοὺς ἔχοντα βληθῆναι εἰς τὴν γέενναν τοῦ πυρός.
paragraphs.translit: kai ei ho ophthalmos sou skandalizei se, exele auton kai bale apo sou· kalon soi estin monophthalmon eis tēn zōēn eiselthein, ē dyo ophthalmous echonta blēthēnai eis tēn geennan tou pyros.

paragraphs.text: See that ye despise not one of these little ones; for I say unto you, that in heaven their angels do always behold the face of my Father who is in heaven.
paragraphs.original: Ὁρᾶτε μὴ καταφρονήσητε ἑνὸς τῶν μικρῶν τούτων, λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν ὅτι οἱ ἄγγελοι αὐτῶν ἐν οὐρανοῖς διὰ παντὸς βλέπουσι τὸ πρόσωπον τοῦ πατρός μου τοῦ ἐν οὐρανοῖς.
paragraphs.translit: Horate mē kataphronēsēte henos tōn mikrōn toutōn, legō gar hymin hoti hoi angeloi autōn en ouranois dia pantos blepousi to prosōpon tou patros mou tou en ouranois.

paragraphs.text: [For the Son of man came to save that which was lost.]
How think ye? if any man have a hundred sheep, and one of them be gone astray, doth he not leave the ninety and nine, and go unto the mountains, and seek that which goeth astray?
paragraphs.original: τί ὑμῖν δοκεῖ; ἐὰν γένηταί τινι ἀνθρώπῳ ἑκατὸν πρόβατα καὶ πλανηθῇ ἓν ἐξ αὐτῶν, οὐχὶ ἀφήσει τὰ ἐνενήκοντα ἐννέα ἐπὶ τὰ ὄρη καὶ πορευθεὶς ζητεῖ τὸ πλανώμενον;
paragraphs.translit: ti hymin dokei; ean genētai tini anthrōpō hekaton probata kai planēthē hen ex autōn, ouchi aphēsei ta enenēkonta ennea epi ta orē kai poreutheis zētei to planōmenon;

paragraphs.text: And if so be that he find it, verily I say unto you, he rejoiceth over it more than over the ninety and nine which have not gone astray.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐὰν γένηται εὑρεῖν αὐτό, ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι χαίρει ἐπʼ αὐτῷ μᾶλλον ἢ ἐπὶ τοῖς ἐνενήκοντα ἐννέα τοῖς μὴ πεπλανημένοις.
paragraphs.translit: kai ean genētai heurein auto, amēn legō hymin hoti chairei epʼ autō mallon ē epi tois enenēkonta ennea tois mē peplanēmenois.

paragraphs.text: Even so it is not the will of your Father who is in heaven, that one of these little ones should perish.
paragraphs.original: οὕτως οὐκ ἔστιν θέλημα ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ πατρὸς ὑμῶν τοῦ ἐν οὐρανοῖς ἵνα ἀπόληται ἓν τῶν μικρῶν τούτων.
paragraphs.translit: houtōs ouk estin thelēma emprosthen tou patros hymōn tou en ouranois hina apolētai hen tōn mikrōn toutōn.

paragraphs.text: And if thy brother sin against thee, go, show him his fault between thee and him alone: if he hear thee, thou hast gained thy brother.
paragraphs.original: Ἐὰν δὲ ἁμαρτήσῃ εἰς σὲ ὁ ἀδελφός σου, ὕπαγε ἔλεγξον αὐτὸν μεταξὺ σοῦ καὶ αὐτοῦ μόνου. ἐάν σου ἀκούσῃ, ἐκέρδησας τὸν ἀδελφόν σου·
paragraphs.translit: Ean de hamartēsē eis se ho adelphos sou, hypage elenxon auton metaxy sou kai autou monou. ean sou akousē, ekerdēsas ton adelphon sou·

paragraphs.text: But if he hear [thee] not, take with thee one or two more, that at the mouth of two witnesses or three every word may be established.
paragraphs.original: ἐὰν δὲ μὴ ἀκούσῃ, παράλαβε μετὰ σοῦ ἔτι ἕνα ἢ δύο, ἵνα ἐπὶ στόματος δύο μαρτύρων ἢ τριῶν σταθῇ πᾶν ῥῆμα·
paragraphs.translit: ean de mē akousē, paralabe meta sou eti hena ē dyo, hina epi stomatos dyo martyrōn ē triōn stathē pan rhēma·

paragraphs.text: And if he refuse to hear them, tell it unto the church: and if he refuse to hear the church also, let him be unto thee as the Gentile and the publican.
paragraphs.original: ἐὰν δὲ παρακούσῃ αὐτῶν, εἰπὸν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ· ἐὰν δὲ καὶ τῆς ἐκκλησίας παρακούσῃ, ἔστω σοι ὥσπερ ὁ ἐθνικὸς καὶ ὁ τελώνης.
paragraphs.translit: ean de parakousē autōn, eipon tē ekklēsia· ean de kai tēs ekklēsias parakousē, estō soi hōsper ho ethnikos kai ho telōnēs.

paragraphs.text: Verily I say unto you, what things soever ye shall bind on earth shall be bound in heaven; and what things soever ye shall loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven.
paragraphs.original: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ὅσα ἐὰν δήσητε ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἔσται δεδεμένα ἐν οὐρανῷ καὶ ὅσα ἐὰν λύσητε ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἔσται λελυμένα ἐν οὐρανῷ.
paragraphs.translit: amēn legō hymin, hosa ean dēsēte epi tēs gēs estai dedemena en ouranō kai hosa ean lysēte epi tēs gēs estai lelymena en ouranō.

paragraphs.text: Again I say unto you, that if two of you shall agree on earth as touching anything that they shall ask, it shall be done for them of my Father who is in heaven.
paragraphs.original: Πάλιν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ἐὰν δύο συμφωνήσωσιν ἐξ ὑμῶν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς περὶ παντὸς πράγματος οὗ ἐὰν αἰτήσωνται, γενήσεται αὐτοῖς παρὰ τοῦ πατρός μου τοῦ ἐν οὐρανοῖς.
paragraphs.translit: Palin amēn legō hymin hoti ean dyo symphōnēsōsin ex hymōn epi tēs gēs peri pantos pragmatos hou ean aitēsōntai, genēsetai autois para tou patros mou tou en ouranois.

paragraphs.text: For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them.
paragraphs.original: οὗ γάρ εἰσιν δύο ἢ τρεῖς συνηγμένοι εἰς τὸ ἐμὸν ὄνομα, ἐκεῖ εἰμι ἐν μέσῳ αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: hou gar eisin dyo ē treis synēgmenoi eis to emon onoma, ekei eimi en mesō autōn.

paragraphs.text: Then came Peter and said to him, Lord, how oft shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? until seven times?
paragraphs.original: Τότε προσελθὼν αὐτῷ ὁ Πέτρος εἶπεν· Κύριε, ποσάκις ἁμαρτήσει εἰς ἐμὲ ὁ ἀδελφός μου καὶ ἀφήσω αὐτῷ; ἕως ἑπτάκις;
paragraphs.translit: Tote proselthōn autō ho Petros eipen· Kyrie, posakis hamartēsei eis eme ho adelphos mou kai aphēsō autō; heōs heptakis;

paragraphs.text: Jesus saith unto him, I say not unto thee, Until seven times; but, Until seventy times seven.
paragraphs.original: λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Οὐ λέγω σοι ἕως ἑπτάκις ἀλλὰ ἕως ἑβδομηκοντάκις ἑπτά.
paragraphs.translit: legei autō ho Iēsous· Ou legō soi heōs heptakis alla heōs hebdomēkontakis hepta.

paragraphs.text: Therefore is the kingdom of heaven likened unto a certain king, who would make a reckoning with his servants.
paragraphs.original: Διὰ τοῦτο ὡμοιώθη ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν ἀνθρώπῳ βασιλεῖ ὃς ἠθέλησεν συνᾶραι λόγον μετὰ τῶν δούλων αὐτοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: Dia touto hōmoiōthē hē basileia tōn ouranōn anthrōpō basilei hos ēthelēsen synarai logon meta tōn doulōn autou·

paragraphs.text: And when he had begun to reckon, one was brought unto him, that owed him ten thousand talents.
paragraphs.original: ἀρξαμένου δὲ αὐτοῦ συναίρειν προσηνέχθη αὐτῷ εἷς ὀφειλέτης μυρίων ταλάντων.
paragraphs.translit: arxamenou de autou synairein prosēnechthē autō heis opheiletēs myriōn talantōn.

paragraphs.text: But forasmuch as he had not [wherewith] to pay, his lord commanded him to be sold, and his wife, and children, and all that he had, and payment to be made.
paragraphs.original: μὴ ἔχοντος δὲ αὐτοῦ ἀποδοῦναι ἐκέλευσεν αὐτὸν ὁ κύριος πραθῆναι καὶ τὴν γυναῖκα καὶ τὰ τέκνα καὶ πάντα ὅσα ἔχει καὶ ἀποδοθῆναι.
paragraphs.translit: mē echontos de autou apodounai ekeleusen auton ho kyrios prathēnai kai tēn gynaika kai ta tekna kai panta hosa echei kai apodothēnai.

paragraphs.text: The servant therefore fell down and worshipped him, saying, Lord, have patience with me, and I will pay thee all.
paragraphs.original: πεσὼν οὖν ὁ δοῦλος προσεκύνει αὐτῷ λέγων· Μακροθύμησον ἐπʼ ἐμοί, καὶ πάντα ἀποδώσω σοι.
paragraphs.translit: pesōn oun ho doulos prosekynei autō legōn· Makrothymēson epʼ emoi, kai panta apodōsō soi.

paragraphs.text: And the lord of that servant, being moved with compassion, released him, and forgave him the debt.
paragraphs.original: σπλαγχνισθεὶς δὲ ὁ κύριος τοῦ δούλου ἐκείνου ἀπέλυσεν αὐτόν, καὶ τὸ δάνειον ἀφῆκεν αὐτῷ.
paragraphs.translit: splanchnistheis de ho kyrios tou doulou ekeinou apelysen auton, kai to daneion aphēken autō.

paragraphs.text: But that servant went out, and found one of his fellow-servants, who owed him a hundred shillings: and he laid hold on him, and took [him] by the throat, saying, Pay what thou owest.
paragraphs.original: ἐξελθὼν δὲ ὁ δοῦλος ἐκεῖνος εὗρεν ἕνα τῶν συνδούλων αὐτοῦ ὃς ὤφειλεν αὐτῷ ἑκατὸν δηνάρια, καὶ κρατήσας αὐτὸν ἔπνιγεν λέγων· Ἀπόδος εἴ τι ὀφείλεις.
paragraphs.translit: exelthōn de ho doulos ekeinos heuren hena tōn syndoulōn autou hos ōpheilen autō hekaton dēnaria, kai kratēsas auton epnigen legōn· Apodos ei ti opheileis.

paragraphs.text: So his fellow-servant fell down and besought him, saying, Have patience with me, and I will pay thee.
paragraphs.original: πεσὼν οὖν ὁ σύνδουλος αὐτοῦ παρεκάλει αὐτὸν λέγων· Μακροθύμησον ἐπʼ ἐμοί, καὶ ἀποδώσω σοι.
paragraphs.translit: pesōn oun ho syndoulos autou parekalei auton legōn· Makrothymēson epʼ emoi, kai apodōsō soi.

paragraphs.text: And he would not: but went and cast him into prison, till he should pay that which was due.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ οὐκ ἤθελεν, ἀλλὰ ἀπελθὼν ἔβαλεν αὐτὸν εἰς φυλακὴν ἕως οὗ ἀποδῷ τὸ ὀφειλόμενον.
paragraphs.translit: ho de ouk ēthelen, alla apelthōn ebalen auton eis phylakēn heōs hou apodō to opheilomenon.

paragraphs.text: So when his fellow-servants saw what was done, they were exceeding sorry, and came and told unto their lord all that was done.
paragraphs.original: ἰδόντες οὖν οἱ σύνδουλοι αὐτοῦ τὰ γενόμενα ἐλυπήθησαν σφόδρα, καὶ ἐλθόντες διεσάφησαν τῷ κυρίῳ ἑαυτῶν πάντα τὰ γενόμενα.
paragraphs.translit: idontes oun hoi syndouloi autou ta genomena elypēthēsan sphodra, kai elthontes diesaphēsan tō kyriō heautōn panta ta genomena.

paragraphs.text: Then his lord called him unto him, and saith to him, Thou wicked servant, I forgave thee all that debt, because thou besoughtest me:
paragraphs.original: τότε προσκαλεσάμενος αὐτὸν ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ λέγει αὐτῷ· Δοῦλε πονηρέ, πᾶσαν τὴν ὀφειλὴν ἐκείνην ἀφῆκά σοι, ἐπεὶ παρεκάλεσάς με·
paragraphs.translit: tote proskalesamenos auton ho kyrios autou legei autō· Doule ponēre, pasan tēn opheilēn ekeinēn aphēka soi, epei parekalesas me·

paragraphs.text: shouldest not thou also have had mercy on thy fellow-servant, even as I had mercy on thee?
paragraphs.original: οὐκ ἔδει καὶ σὲ ἐλεῆσαι τὸν σύνδουλόν σου, ὡς κἀγὼ σὲ ἠλέησα;
paragraphs.translit: ouk edei kai se eleēsai ton syndoulon sou, hōs kagō se ēleēsa;

paragraphs.text: And his lord was wroth, and delivered him to the tormentors, till he should pay all that was due.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὀργισθεὶς ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ παρέδωκεν αὐτὸν τοῖς βασανισταῖς ἕως οὗ ἀποδῷ πᾶν τὸ ὀφειλόμενον.
paragraphs.translit: kai orgistheis ho kyrios autou paredōken auton tois basanistais heōs hou apodō pan to opheilomenon.

paragraphs.text: So shall also my heavenly Father do unto you, if ye forgive not every one his brother from your hearts.
paragraphs.original: Οὕτως καὶ ὁ πατήρ μου ὁ οὐράνιος ποιήσει ὑμῖν ἐὰν μὴ ἀφῆτε ἕκαστος τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ τῶν καρδιῶν ὑμῶν.
paragraphs.translit: Houtōs kai ho patēr mou ho ouranios poiēsei hymin ean mē aphēte hekastos tō adelphō autou apo tōn kardiōn hymōn.
